author: Joshua Fluke
description:
Companies love lecturing job applicants about honesty while somehow changing the salary, location, schedule, responsibilities, benefits and even the job itself halfway through the hiring process.

An applicant exaggerates something on a resume and suddenly it’s an integrity problem.

Meanwhile, a company can advertise an $80,000–$100,000 salary, drag you through multiple interviews and then send you an offer for $62,000 because apparently “the approved budget changed.”

A remote job can slowly become hybrid and then five days a week in the office.

A senior position can suddenly become junior — while keeping the senior responsibilities.

A temporary position that was “basically guaranteed” to become permanent can stay temporary indefinitely.

A promotion can become an undefined future possibility.

Training can become a folder of outdated documents and a coworker who doesn’t have time to help you.

Unlimited PTO can turn into unlimited conversations about why you can’t actually take P
title: HOW CEOS LEGALLY LIE TO JOB APPLICANTS
